title: Efficacy and safety of single-fraction stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) for the curative treatment of extracranial primary Tumors: A collaborative systematic review on behalf of the SBRT Focus Group of the European Society for Radiotherapy & Oncology (ESTRO).
authors: Cuccia F, Franzese C, Dubash S, Dionisi V, Brunner T, Cellini F, Hörner-Rieber J, Zilli T
abstract: Single-fraction stereotactic body radiotherapy (SF-SBRT) represents one of the most advanced frontiers in modern radiation oncology. While ultra-hypofractionation has entered everyday clinical practice in different fields of the oncological care, curative treatments in one session are increasingly attractive for the potential favorable combination of logistic advantages with safety and clinical outcomes. This collaborative systematic review promoted by the ESTRO SBRT Focus Group in participation with members of different disease-site Focus Groups collects the available data in support of SF-SBRT for the curative treatment of the main extracranial primary tumors. The findings highlight that, for specific anatomical sites, SF-SBRT is both safe and effective though the results emphasize the critical importance of careful patient selection and mandatory technological requirements for treatment planning and delivery. This collaborative work provides a comprehensive overview of current evidence and identifies key knowledge gaps for future investigation and upcoming clinical trials.

title: Predicting IGD treatment outcomes across interventions using a whole-brain functional connectome biomarker.
authors: Wei M, Luo X, Fu J, Li S, Ni H, Liu J, Dong GH
abstract: BACKGROUND: Although treatment approaches have been explored in internet gaming disorder (IGD), however, little is known about the specific neural activity that is associated with treatment outcomes. This study aims to establish a treatment-sensitive network that reliably predicts treatment outcomes across different interventions for IGD. METHODS: Resting-state fMRI data were collected from 90 individuals with IGD who received one of three different intervention protocols (mindfulness meditation, approach bias modification, or retrieval-aversive conditioning training). Connectome-based predictive modelling (CPM) was used to build a treatment-sensitive network to predict individual symptom reduction, then validated them on the external dataset. RESULTS: The negative (r = 0.401, p <.001) and combined network (r = 0.480, p <.001) can significantly predict a reduction of addiction severity (baseline minus post-test). Specifically, the negative network was primarily centred on the motor, subcortical, and salience networks. The positive network primarily involved cerebellar-related connections. Incorporating these into a combined model significantly improved predictive accuracy, suggesting that cerebellar-related connectivity may contribute to the prediction of intervention-related clinical improvement. Finally, the treatment-sensitive network was validated in a separate data. CONCLUSIONS: This study established a treatment-sensitive network based on the whole-brain connectome. These findings provide valuable empirical evidence for identifying biomarkers for IGD treatment and advance personalised therapeutic strategies. CLINICAL TRIALS REGISTRATION: The trial protocol was pre-registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (www.chictr.org.cn; ChiCTR2300077831(MM), ChiCTR2300075869(ApBm), ChiCTR2500095444(R-AC), ChiCTR2400090834(SAE)).

title: Liver fibrosis risk, missed follow-up, and inequitable specialist referral in the All of Us Research Program: a retrospective cohort study.
authors: Sellers K, White TM, Manolas MI, Hagström H, Brennan PN, Diaz LA, Bansal MB, Danpanichkul P
abstract: BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is highly prevalent and frequently undiagnosed, despite liver fibrosis being the strongest predictor of liver-related morbidity and mortality. We aimed to quantify Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index-based fibrosis risk and to evaluate guideline-recommended follow-up-FIB-4 documentation, confirmatory testing, and specialist referral-in a large US cohort. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study of electronic health record data from the US All of Us Research Program. Among adults aged 35 years or older with sufficient laboratory data, FIB-4 scores were calculated from routinely captured biomarkers, classified as low (<1.3), indeterminate (1.3-2.67; 2.0-2.67 if aged ≥65 years), or high risk (>2.67), and described across sociodemographic and metabolic subgroups; associations with incident major adverse liver outcomes (MALO) were assessed with Cox proportional-hazards regression. We examined FIB-4 documentation, confirmatory testing, and specialty referrals within 365 days of the index FIB-4 date. FINDINGS: Among 136,004 participants (mean age 60.8 years [SD 13.5]; 79,365 [58.4%] female; 81,420 [59.9%] White, 21,779 [16.0%] Hispanic or Latino, 20,076 [14.8%] Black), 26,971 (19.8%, 95% CI 19.6-20.0) had indeterminate and 11,217 (8.2%, 8.1-8.4) high FIB-4-based fibrosis risk. Elevated risk was more frequent with cardiovascular disease (41.7% vs 25.6%), hypertension (30.7% vs 23.4%), and type 2 diabetes (29.7% vs 27.4%), rising from 25.6% with no metabolic comorbidities to 36.6% with four. FIB-4 documentation was rare, and fewer than 1% of high-risk participants underwent confirmatory testing or referral; referral was low across risk categories (0.19% high, 0.19% indeterminate, 0.25% low risk). MALO occurred in 1308 (11.7%) high-risk vs 830 (0.8%) low-risk participants (adjusted hazard ratio 19.68, 95% CI 17.88-21.67). INTERPRETATION: Routinely collected laboratory data identify substantial liver fibrosis risk in this volunteer US cohort, yet guideline-recommended follow-up is uncommon. Implementation strategies such as automated risk calculation and reflex-based testing pathways could reduce missed opportunities for earlier diagnosis and intervention. FUNDING: No specific funding was received for this study.

title: Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic syndrome and suicidal death in a nationwide cohort study.
authors: Huh H, Kang MW, Lee J, Oh J, Kim M, Koh JH, Kwon JK, Cho JM
abstract: BACKGROUND: Individual cardiometabolic diseases are associated with psychiatric conditions and suicide. However, the association between the recently proposed Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic (CKM) syndrome framework and suicide-related mortality remains unevaluated. METHODS: We analyzed data from 4,601,001 participants in the Korean National Health Insurance Service database, categorizing CKM health into Stages 0-4. The association between CKM stages and suicide-related mortality was evaluated using multivariable Cox regression with sequential adjustment for clinicodemographic variables, comorbidity, and claims-based psychiatric diagnoses, and using Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard models treating non-suicide death as a competing event. RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 10.11 years, 12,034 suicidal death events occurred. After adjustment, advanced CKM stages were associated with an increased risk of suicidal death (stage 3: adjusted HR 1.328, 95% CI 1.217-1.449; stage 4: adjusted HR 1.319, 95% CI 1.220-1.426), and the association persisted after further adjustment for other psychiatric disorders. Estimates were attenuated but remained significant in Fine-Gray models accounting for the competing risk of non-suicide death (stage 3: subdistribution HR 1.199, 95% CI 1.098-1.310; stage 4: 1.246, 95% CI 1.150-1.349). Exploratory subgroup analyses indicated that the association was most pronounced in younger adults aged 20-39 and in individuals without a claims-based diagnosis of depression. CONCLUSIONS: Advanced CKM syndrome is associated with increased suicide-related mortality. Mental health surveillance within the clinical management of CKM dysfunction may serve as a potential preventive strategy. Future studies are needed to evaluate the utility of CKM-based risk stratification in suicidal death prevention.

title: Evaluating a Modified American Society of Anesthesiologists Physical Status-Based Sedation Management System for Pancreatobiliary Endoscopy: A Prospective Feasibility Study.
authors: Hanaoka T, Okuwaki K, Watanabe M, Matsuda H, Adachi K, Tamaki A, Ogawa D, Sakai M
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To prospectively evaluate the feasibility of implementing a modified American Society of Anesthesiologists Physical Status (ASA-PS)-based sedation management system for endoscopist-managed sedation in pancreatobiliary endoscopy. METHODS: This single-center, single-arm prospective feasibility study involved 2000 patients (2024-2025). Sedation risk was stratified using a modified ASA-PS classification system combined with predefined high-risk clinical factors (severe obesity, obstructive sleep apnea requiring continuous positive airway pressure, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease requiring home oxygen therapy, reduced functional capacity, and difficult sedation history). Patients meeting high-risk criteria underwent pre-procedural anesthesiologist assessment to determine sedation providers. The primary outcome was sedation-related adverse event (SRAE) incidence during endoscopist-managed sedation. The secondary outcomes were the sedation success rate and SRAE-associated risk factors. RESULTS: Among 2000 patients, 231 (11.6%) were classified as having high risk for sedation. Post-assessment, anesthesiologists and endoscopists managed sedation for 86 (4.3%) and 1914 (95.7%) patients, respectively. In the endoscopist-managed group, SRAEs occurred in 63 patients (3.3%), corresponding to a success rate of 96.7%. No patient required tracheal intubation or conversion to general anesthesia. In multivariable analysis, endoscopic ultrasonography-guided sampling was independently associated with reduced SRAEs (odds ratio 0.407, 95% confidence interval 0.184-0.899; p = 0.026); no independent predictors of increased SRAEs were identified. CONCLUSIONS: The modified ASA-PS-based sedation management system may be a feasible approach in settings with limited anesthesiology resources, warranting further validation. TRIAL REGISTRATION: UMIN000053211.

title: Microenvironmental barriers to healing in osteoradionecrosis and opportunities for regenerative intervention.
authors: La Croix AE, Torres Gouveia ME, Bertone PM, Nemanic NM, Bahney CS, Hixon KR
abstract: Osteoradionecrosis (ORN) is a debilitating sequela of radiotherapy (RT) for head and neck cancer (HNC), characterized by persistent bone exposure or radiographic non-viability and profound tissue repair failure. Despite advances in radiation delivery and clinical management, ORN remains challenging to treat, with therapeutic strategies largely focused on symptom control, infection mitigation, or surgical reconstruction rather than restoration of regenerative capacity. Emerging evidence suggests that radiation-induced cellular senescence represents a central and underrecognized driver of ORN pathophysiology. Ionizing radiation disrupts the bone microenvironment through sustained vascular injury, impaired osteogenic-angiogenic coupling, chronic inflammation, and the accumulation of senescent bone-resident and stromal cells that secrete a pro-inflammatory senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP). Together, these changes create a hostile niche that suppresses bone remodeling and wound healing long after radiation exposure. This review synthesizes current understanding of radiation-induced injury to the bone microenvironment, critically evaluates existing classification systems and treatment strategies for ORN, and examines emerging regenerative approaches. We further propose senotherapeutic strategies targeting radiation-induced cellular senescence as a complementary and potentially transformative avenue to restore tissue repair capacity. By integrating regenerative biomaterials with targeted modulation of senescence, future therapies may move beyond palliation toward true biological resolution of ORN. Biomaterial delivery systems (e.g., injectable hydrogels, mineral composite scaffolds, and cryogel platforms) are emerging as promising vehicles for spatiotemporally controlled senotherapeutic delivery within the irradiated bone niche.

title: Gut microbiota shaping fatty liver disease progression.
authors: Wysokińska M, Mysza M, Uryga AE, Kołodziejczyk AA
abstract: The gut-liver axis is an important regulator of homeostasis, and its dysregulation has been implicated in the pathogenesis of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). In this review, we summarize current knowledge on both compositional alterations of the gut microbiome in MASLD and the functional consequences of these changes. We first discuss changes across major microbial domains, including bacteria, archaea, eukaryota, and bacteriophages, and then focus on microbiota-derived metabolites, such as short-chain fatty acids, trimethylamine and its derivative trimethylamine N-oxide, tryptophan-derived indoles, secondary bile acids, and other bioactive compounds. Their complex impacts on intestinal barrier integrity, inflammation, lipid and glucose metabolism, and immune and hormonal signaling in the liver are highlighted. We further examine mechanisms involving the translocation of microbial products and the modulation of nuclear and membrane receptors. Finally, we outline current challenges and knowledge gaps that need to be addressed to better understand the role of the gut microbiota in MASLD.

title: Pacak-Zhuang syndrome with EPAS1 p.Pro531Leu somatic variant: one case report and literature review.
authors: Li X, Song S, Wang L, Zhong Z, Qi Y, Gong Y
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To report a case child of Pacak-Zhuang syndrome with EPAS1 p.Pro531Leu somatic variant in a child and to summarize the clinical characteristics, diagnosis, treatment methods, and prognosis of this syndrome based on a literature review. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on the clinical data of a child girl with Pacak-Zhuang syndrome admitted to Hebei Children's Hospital in July 2019. Using the search terms 'Pacak-Zhuang syndrome', 'EPAS1', 'HIF-2α', 'HIF-2A', and 'Polycythemia-paraganglioma syndrome', relevant literature was retrieved from PubMed and Web of Science. The clinical manifestations, diagnostic methods, treatment plans, and outcomes of patients with this syndrome were analyzed. RESULTS: A 4-year-old girl had recurrent hypertension, polycythemia and renal hilar masses. Diagnosis was confirmed by imaging, biochemical detection and paraffin tissue genetic testing. She received three operations for paragangliomas; pathology showed CgA(+), Syn(+), NSE(+) and Ki‑67 ≤5%. Follow-up revealed tumor recurrence, but the condition improved with oral temozolomide. Combined with 10 retrieved articles, 18 patients (4 males,14 females, mean age 25 years) were analyzed. Polycythemia was the cardinal manifestation. All patients received surgery, and 10 suffered uncontrolled tumor recurrence. CONCLUSION: Pacak-Zhuang syndrome is a rare disorder involving the neuroendocrine and hematopoietic systems, often initially presenting with 'polycythemia'. Most cases are sporadic, with no apparent familial inheritance or history of other neuroendocrine tumors. When encountering pediatric patients with unexplained hypertension accompanied by polycythemia symptoms, the possibility of this syndrome should be considered, and further imaging studies and genetic testing are required for definitive diagnosis.

title: Therapeutic Balloon-Assisted Enteroscopy: Recent Advances in the Management of Small Bowel Diseases.
authors: Nagayama M, Kinoshita T, Kawaguchi H, Fujinuma T, Fujikura S, Hayashi H, Tamaru T, Sakamoto H
abstract: Balloon-assisted enteroscopy (BAE) has substantially advanced small bowel disease management. This review summarizes recent therapeutic BAE advances, focusing on three major indications: small bowel vascular lesions, hereditary polyposis syndromes, and Crohn's disease (CD). For suspected small bowel bleeding from vascular lesions, morphological classification guides lesion-specific hemostasis-primarily using argon plasma coagulation and clipping-while gel immersion endoscopy helps secure the visual field. In hereditary polyposis syndromes (e.g., Peutz-Jeghers syndrome and familial adenomatous polyposis), endoscopic ischemic and cold snare polypectomy prevent intussusception and reduce cancer risk, decreasing surgical needs. Additionally, endoscopic balloon dilation is an established bowel-preserving treatment for fibrotic CD strictures, reducing surgical resection and short bowel syndrome risk. Driven by evolving imaging and devices, BAE remains central to small bowel management, improving patient outcomes and quality of life.

title: Targeting the lactate/P300/H3K18la epigenetic pathway with a mechanoadaptive biomimetic hydrogel to suppress traumatic tendon heterotopic ossification.
authors: Feng H, Ang K, Deng Z, Cui C, Chen J, Huang N, Feng Y, Zhang J
abstract: Traumatic heterotopic ossification (HO) is a debilitating complication of tendon injury, yet its pathogenic mechanisms remain elusive and effective preventive strategies are lacking. Here, we identify a glycometabolic-epigenetic axis that drives HO progression. Single-cell profiling and functional analyses reveal that hypoxic chondrocytes undergo glycolytic reprogramming, leading to lactate accumulation and transfer into tendon-derived mesenchymal stem cells (TD-MSCs) through MCT1. This metabolic coupling promotes P300-dependent histone H3 lysine 18 lactylation (H3K18la), activating osteogenic programs characterized by Col6a1, Zhx3, Lox and Vdr expression and thereby facilitating pathological endochondral ossification. Guided by this mechanism, we develop a tendon-adhesive hydrogel (GelHA-A485@Exos) that integrates mechanical repair with targeted epigenetic modulation. MSC-derived exosomes enable localized delivery of the P300 inhibitor A485, suppressing H3K18la and aberrant osteogenic activation, while the hydrogel scaffold enhances tendon regeneration. In vivo and in vitro studies demonstrate that GelHA-A485@Exos promotes tendon healing while preventing HO formation. Our findings establish metabolic-epigenetic communication as a central regulator of traumatic HO and provide a translational therapeutic strategy for its clinical prevention.

title: Neuroimaging Biomarkers for Brain Disorder Diagnosis Using Advanced Learning Techniques.
authors: Ion IA, Chira C
abstract: Mental illness is becoming increasingly common in everyday life, affecting a growing number of people. Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI) is an effective technique for detecting mental disorders. Resting-state fMRI (rs-fMRI) analyses spontaneous low-frequency oscillations in the Blood Oxygen Level Dependent signal to examine the functional architecture of the brain. fMRI and rs-fMRI data processing contribute to mapping neural activity in specific brain regions, enabling accurate localization of cognitive functions and improving our understanding of Functional Connectivity and interactions among brain regions. This paper focuses on the use of Machine Learning and Deep Learning techniques for fMRI analysis to identify brain features that may be associated with Bipolar Disorder (BD) and Alzheimer's Disease (AD). The first step in the proposed approach is the preprocessing of fMRI and rs-fMRI data using two distinct methods: the first combines Statistical Parametric Mapping and the CONN toolbox for improved results, and the second focuses on the MELODIC software. The proposed approach begins with fMRI and rs-fMRI preprocessing using two pipelines: one integrating Statistical Parametric Mapping (SPM) with the CONN toolbox and another based on the MELODIC framework. The aim is to evaluate how preprocessing choices affect functional connectivity representations and classification performance when combined with classical Machine Learning (ML) methods, namely Support Vector Machines and Random Forests, and the Deep Learning (DL) model AlexNet. Given the altered brain connectivity patterns observed in Bipolar Disorder and Alzheimer's Disease, these methods are employed to assess preprocessing-learning interactions across both disorders. Experimental results emphasize that Connbox-SPM preprocessing combined with AlexNet yields the best results for both mental disorders, with Bipolar Disorder reporting 78.2% accuracy and AD achieving 82.4% accuracy.

title: Discovering Heterogeneous Neurodegenerative Disease Patterns From MRI Data for Improved Prediction.
authors: Zhang Y, Li H, Fan Y
journal: Medical image computing and computer-assisted intervention : MICCAI ... International Conference on Medical Image Computing and Computer-Assisted Intervention
abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases exhibit substantial heterogeneity, complicating both diagnosis and prognosis. Identifying clinically meaningful subtypes is crucial for understanding disease mechanisms and improving diagnostic precision and prognostic accuracy. Existing subtyping approaches primarily rely on unsupervised learning of patient data for capturing inter-individual variability, but they may fail to uncover subtypes that are directly informative for diagnosis or prognosis. To address this limitation, we propose a novel mixture-of-experts (MoE) framework that integrates predictive modeling with subtype discovery. Unlike traditional subtyping methods, our approach learns a router to assign individuals to specialized expert networks, each corresponding to a distinct subtype, for improving predictive accuracy. By coupling subtype identification with prediction, the proposed MoE framework encourages the discovery of subtypes that are not only statistically distinct but also clinically informative. We evaluate the framework on a real-world dataset of mild cognitive impairment (MCI) subjects and a semi-simulated dataset, demonstrating superior performance in predicting progression from MCI to Alzheimer's disease while revealing distinct, clinically meaningful MCI subtypes. Code is available at https://github.com/Kateridge/MoESubtyping.

title: Janus-structured piezoelectric membrane couples barrier protection with pathological microenvironment-responsive bioactivity for periodontal bone regeneration.
authors: Chen C, Sun J, Fang K, Miao W, Du X, Li J, Wen X, Qu Z
abstract: Periodontal bone regeneration remains challenging due to the persistent infection-inflammation-bone resorption cycle and the rapid invasion of epithelial and gingival connective tissues into defect sites. Here, we developed a biodegradable Janus membrane (J-PLLA-ZnO) based on poly(L-lactic acid) (PLLA) that spatially integrates barrier protection and pH-responsive bioactivity within a single construct. A dense PLLA layer facing soft tissues prevents premature tissue infiltration and maintains regenerative space, while a porous defect-facing interface functionalized with ZnO nanowires provides bioactive regulation. The ZnO nanowires enhance the overall piezoelectric response of the membrane and enable pH-responsive Zn2+ release under the acidic periodontal microenvironment, thereby delivering antibacterial, immunomodulatory, and osteogenic cues. In a rat periodontitis model, J-PLLA-ZnO rapidly suppressed infection-associated inflammation. One week after implantation, peripheral neutrophil percentage decreased to approximately 21% of those in the J-PLLA group, accompanied by reduced tumor necrosis factor-α expression and increased cluster of differentiation 206 expression, consistent with a shift toward a reparative macrophage phenotype. At week 6, J-PLLA-ZnO increased the osteocalcin-positive bone-forming area by approximately 1.5-fold compared with non-Janus PLLA-ZnO, indicating improved periodontal bone regeneration. Moreover, the cementoenamel junction-alveolar bone crest distance was reduced by approximately 40% relative to untreated controls. Meanwhile, the membrane underwent gradual biodegradation throughout the healing process. These findings demonstrate that integrating spatial barrier function with pH-responsive bioactivity represents a promising strategy for guided tissue regeneration in inflammatory periodontal defects.

title: Surface-modified 3D-printed sphene scaffolds for photothermal osteosarcoma therapy and osteogenic stimulation.
authors: Bigham A, Hu X, Mariano A, Ventre M, Serrano-Ruiz M, Yang X, Zhang X, Bemporad E
abstract: Bone cancer treatment following surgical resection requires the elimination of residual tumor cells while promoting the regeneration of tumor-associated bone defects. Here, we developed a hierarchically surface-engineered, 3D-printed sphene scaffold (SPH, CaTiSiO5) integrating photothermal tumor ablation with osteogenic-supportive properties. Scaffolds fabricated from sol-gel-derived SPH powder were sequentially modified with an ordered mesoporous bioactive glass (OMBG) coating and a black phosphorus-polydopamine (BP-PD) nanocomposite. OMBG promoted calcium phosphate-rich mineral deposition and osteogenic differentiation and also displayed NIR-induced heating, while the subsequent BP-PD deposition further increased the photothermal response and tumor-cell ablation. In vitro, the modified scaffolds showed favorable cytocompatibility, enhanced osteogenic differentiation of human mesenchymal stem cells, and efficient photothermal killing of K7M2 osteosarcoma cells. In a rabbit distal femoral VX2 malignant bone tumor model, the scaffold significantly suppressed local tumor growth and invasion, reduced systemic tumor-associated deterioration and distant organ metastasis, and improved therapeutic outcomes without detectable systemic cytotoxicity. 3D MRI-CT fusion reconstruction confirmed reductions in solid tumor volume, peritumoral edema, and intramedullary invasion, demonstrating effective local tumor control and preservation of peri-implant bone within a single implantable therapeutic system. These findings establish surface-engineered SPH scaffolds as a multifunctional platform that combines effective local tumor control and preservation of peri-implant bone in vivo with osteogenic-supportive activity demonstrated in vitro.

title: Gut microbiota and metabolic characteristics in PWHIV with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD).
authors: Liu H, Xu T, Guo Y, Zhou X, Yan C, Zhu B, Xie Y
abstract: The global prevalence of Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) among persons with HIV (PWHIV) is estimated at 34%. This study examined the influence of gut microbial and metabolic alterations in PWHIV with MASLD. We conducted 16S rRNA sequencing on 60 fecal samples (24 from HIV group and 36 from HIV-MASLD group) to assess microbial composition, and employed LC/MS-based metabolomics on both fecal and plasma samples to identify variations in metabolites. An exploratory analysis was performed to compare plasma cytokines and oxidative stress markers between the two groups. Sequencing in the HIV-MASLD group showed lower Faecalibacterium and Anaerobutyricum, and higher Klebsiella, Escherichia, and Enterococcus. Metabolomic analysis revealed a reduction in anti-inflammatory metabolites (Dodecanedioic acid, 5-Phenylvaleric acid, Kynurenic acid) and antioxidant metabolites, coupled with an increase in the pro-inflammatory metabolite Gamma-Glutamyl-L-Putrescine in the HIV-MASLD group. And plasma analysis indicated a decline in 20-carboxy arachidonic acid. Additionally, Faecalibacterium and Anaerobutyricum correlated positively with anti-inflammatory metabolites, while Klebsiella, Enterobacter, and Citrobacter correlated negatively. Furthermore, Faecalibacterium and Anaerobutyricum also showed a moderate negative correlation with MDA levels. A random forest model using plasma metabolites showed the optimal discriminative ability for HIV-MASLD (AUC = 0.819 ± 0.0059). Differences in gut microbiota and metabolites in PWHIV may affect MASLD progression by influencing inflammation and oxidative stress. Modulating gut microbiota, such as adding Faecalibacterium and Anaerobutyricum, could be a treatment strategy for HIV-MASLD. Plasma metabolites have potential as noninvasive markers.

title: Hematopoietic cell transplantation using treosulfan-based conditioning for IL-10 receptor deficiency.
authors: Lakkaraja M, Schmitt EG, Sood AK, Chen K, Modi AJ, Verbsky JW, Torgerson T, Wahbeh G
abstract: IL-10 receptor deficiency is a life-threatening inborn error of immunity associated with early-onset inflammatory bowel disease. Hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) using treosulfan-based conditioning resulted in excellent survival with full donor engraftment. Importantly, anakinra effectively served as a bridge to HCT.

Circulatory arrest versus aortic cross-clamping in proximal thoracic aortic aneurysm repair.
authors: Braatz E, Stenman M, Al-Mousli J, Dalén M, Olsson C
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Aortic cross‑clamping and mild hypothermic circulatory arrest (MHCA) are commonly used strategies in proximal thoracic aortic aneurysm surgery. This study compared these approaches in elective procedures for patients with a distal ascending aortic diameter of 40-50 mm. The primary outcome was a composite of 30‑day mortality, stroke, or acute kidney injury, with secondary outcomes including long‑term survival and postoperative complications. MATERIAL AND METHODS: This single‑center observational cohort included patients treated between 2016 and 2024. Distal ascending aortic diameters were assessed on preoperative computed tomography, and clinical data were obtained from SWEDEHEART. Patients were assigned to aortic cross‑clamp (n = 261) or MHCA (n = 138). Propensity score matching was performed in a 1:1 ratio to balance baseline characteristics. RESULTS: The composite primary outcome occurred in 15 patients (3.8%) and was more common with MHCA than with cross‑clamp (6.5% vs 2.3%, p = 0.035). Two patients (0.5%), both in the MHCA group, died within 30 days. After matching, the odds ratio for the composite endpoint was 2.4 (95% CI, 0.66-11.5), indicating no significant difference. Long‑term survival was similar between groups (log‑rank p = 0.33). CONCLUSIONS: Both strategies were associated with low perioperative risk and comparable long‑term survival. These results support flexible operative planning, allowing the distal anastomotic technique to be chosen based on individual anatomy and surgical preference.

title: Integrated analysis identifies dysregulated secretory proteins and crotonylation profiles associated with immune regulation in IgA nephropathy.
authors: Chen J, Zhang W, Dai Y, Ma H, Ma J, Zou G, Yan Q, Hu G
abstract: BACKGROUND: Immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN) is the most prevalent primary glomerulonephritis worldwide, with 20%-40% of patients progressing to end-stage renal disease. However, the relationship between peripheral immune alterations and local renal injury, particularly with respect to the abundance patterns and post-translational modification signals of secretory proteins, remains incompletely characterized. METHODS: This study included 48 samples, consisting of renal tissue samples from 7 IgAN patients and 10 controls, and peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from 6 patients with IgAN and 25 controls. Renal tissue and PBMC samples were analyzed by proteomic and crotonylation profiling, respectively. These datasets represent cohort-level feature integration rather than paired multi-omics correlation analyses performed within the same individuals. Immune secretory protein annotations from the Human Protein Atlas supported downstream interpretation. Differential abundance analysis, protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analysis, functional enrichment, transcription factor (TF) prediction, and compound enrichment analysis using the DSigDB and Enrichr platforms were performed to explore molecular features and database-derived compounds associated with IgAN. RESULTS: Compared with the corresponding control groups, 92 differentially abundant secreted proteins and 36 secretory proteins with differential protein-abundance-normalized Kcr signals were identified in IgAN patients. PPI network analysis prioritized FGA, FGB, A2M, APOA1, C3, HP, SERPINA1, APOB, FGG, and TF as exploratory hub candidates, while STAT1, PML, STAT5B, and MYH11 were computationally predicted as candidate upstream TFs. Compound enrichment analysis identified thapsigargin as a database-derived, hypothesis-generating compound related to the secretory protein network in IgAN. CONCLUSIONS: This study provides an integrative characterization of secretory protein abundance and crotonylation patterns in IgA nephropathy. The findings suggest candidate hub proteins and upstream TFs potentially associated with immune dysregulation in IgAN. Despite the limited sample size, these results offer exploratory molecular insights and provide a basis for future mechanistic and experimental studies. SIGNIFICANCE: Secretory proteins may contribute to immune dysregulation and renal injury in immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN), but their abundance patterns and lysine crotonylation (Kcr)-related features remain incompletely characterized. This study integrated renal tissue proteomics, peripheral blood mononuclear cell crotonylomics, public transcriptomics, and Human Protein Atlas annotations at the feature level across independent cohorts. Descriptive fold-change screening yielded 92 HPA-annotated secretory proteins in renal tissue and 36 secretory proteins containing 120 protein-abundance-normalized Kcr sites in peripheral blood mononuclear cells. Network analysis prioritized ten exploratory hub candidates, while STAT1, PML, STAT5B, and MYH11 were computationally prioritized as candidate upstream transcription factors. DSigDB/Enrichr analysis further highlighted thapsigargin as a database-derived enrichment signal for hypothesis generation. These findings provide an exploratory molecular resource for investigating secretory protein abundance and Kcr-related patterns in IgAN. Because the datasets were unpaired and the proteomic and crotonylomic samples were pooled within groups, the results do not establish participant-level cross-tissue relationships, causal regulation, validated biomarkers, or therapeutic efficacy. Larger individual-level cohorts and functional studies are required for validation.

title: Real-world comparative outcomes of first-line immune combinations (ICI-ICI vs ICI-TKI) in metastatic renal cell carcinoma with sarcomatoid features.
authors: Rebuzzi SE, Di Costanzo F, Filippi R, Rescigno P, Fornarini G, Signori A, Masini C, Iacovelli R
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Although first-line immune-based combinations have reshaped the management of metastatic renal cell carcinoma (mRCC), relevant unmet clinical needs remain. Sarcomatoid feature is a negative prognostic factor that confers sensitivity to immunotherapy, yet the optimal ICI combination in this subgroup is still unclear. METHODS: The Meet-URO 33 is an Italian multicenter retrospective/prospective observational study enrolling patients with mRCC receiving first-line systemic therapy in routine clinical practice. In the present sub-analysis, objective response and survival outcomes were compared between ICI-ICI and ICI-TKI regimens in patients with documented sarcomatoid differentiation and IMDC intermediate-/poor-risk disease. RESULTS: Among 1695 patients enrolled from 58 centers, 180 (10.6%) had sRCC and among them, 107 (58.2%) were intermediate-risk and 56 (30.4%) were poor-risk. With a median follow-up of 21.8 months, in the I/P-sRCC population with available data (n = 155), univariable analysis showed longer overall survival (OS) with ICI-ICI compared to ICI-TKI (HR 0.58, p = 0.04). However, in propensity score-weighted analyses, point estimates slightly favored ICI-ICI, but no statistically significant differences were observed for OS, PFS, or ORR. CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world analysis comparing ICI-ICI and ICI-TKI in sarcomatoid mRCC, propensity score-weighted models showed no statistically significant differences between treatment combinations on clinical outcomes. These findings highlight the relevance of baseline disease and patients characteristics in shaping treatment outcomes and confirm the effectiveness of ICI-containing combinations in the treatment of sarcomatoid mRCC.

title: Microbial succession and genome-resolved metabolic functions shape flavor evolution during sauce-flavor Baijiu fermentation.
authors: Niu J, Li W, Chen X, Zhu H, Sun W, Li X, Sun B
abstract: Sauce-flavor Baijiu (SFB) fermentation is characterized by a unique multi-round solid-state process, during which complex microbial succession drives flavor formation. However, the functional differentiation and metabolic mechanisms of microbial communities across successive fermentation rounds remain poorly understood. In this study, the physicochemical properties, microbial assembly, and metabolic profiles of fermented grains (FG) were investigated across seven production rounds (R1-R7). The results revealed that as fermentation rounds progressed, the FG environment evolved toward elevated acidity and reduced pH, driving a directional shift in the microbial community from an initially diverse assemblage to a structure dominated by acid-tolerant Acetilactobacillus, which established pronounced ecological dominance in later rounds. Metabolomic analysis further indicated that this dynamic adjustment of microbial structure drove the evolution of the flavor profile, specifically manifesting as differential accumulation of compounds such as esters, alcohols, and pyrazines across the various rounds. Co-occurrence network analysis demonstrated that positive microbial interactions significantly predominated within the fermentation system, and that community function exhibited a convergent trend as the rounds increased. Furthermore, 158 metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) were recovered, and metabolic reconstruction elucidated the potential contributions of genera such as Pediococcus, Bacillus, and Oceanobacillus to key metabolic pathways, including glycolysis, phenylalanine metabolism, and pyrazine biosynthesis. This work provides important insights into microbial regulation and quality improvement in SFB fermentation.

title: Multi-omics and functional validation profiling reveals the regulatory mechanism of biofilm-forming Tetragenococcus halophilus JY1 in response to salt tolerance.
authors: Zhao C, Sun D, Li S, Lu X, Liu X, Mu Y, Luo L
abstract: Biofilms are crucial for enhancing microbial productivity in industrial applications, yet the mechanisms underlying their stress resistance and formation in functional microorganisms remain inadequately explored. Tetragenococcus halophilus, a halophilic lactic acid bacterium, is widely utilized in traditional fermentation industries; however, research has focused on its planktonic state. To address this gap, this study investigated the molecular mechanisms of biofilm formation in T. halophilus JY1 under low-salt (0.2 M, LS) and high-salt (3 M, HS) stress conditions. Physiological analyses revealed that biofilms protected cellular integrity under LS and HS, as evidenced by marked elevations in ATPase activity and ATP concentration. Furthermore, salt stress altered the abundance and composition of JY1 biofilms. RNA-seq analysis identified upregulation of genes associated with cell surface composition, energy homeostasis, and ion transport. Metabolomic profiling further revealed elevated levels of glycerophospholipids and fatty acids in JY1 under LS and HS. Functional validation further demonstrated that overexpression of ohrR, yodB, isaA, icaA, ruvA, and ctsR significantly promoted biofilm formation in recombinant strains. In addition, exogenous monounsaturated fatty acids (C16:1, C14:1, and C20:1) markedly improved cell survival and biofilm formation under salt stress by modulating membrane lipid composition and enhancing osmotic adaptation. Overall, restructuring of biofilms emerged as a key adaptive strategy for JY1 in response to salinity, while prolonged salt exposure reduced physiological and metabolic activity. This study provides critical insights into the adaptive strategies of biofilm-forming microorganisms and opens new avenues for the application of biofilms in industrial processes.

title: Salt-dependent osmoadaptation and metabolic responses of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum BS3-1 in fermented bamboo shoots.
authors: Xie L, Zhang X, Shen K, Wang X, Zhou S
abstract: Salt concentration shapes the growth and metabolism of lactic acid bacteria in vegetable fermentations, yet the effects of salt gradients on the fermentation performance of suansun-derived Lactiplantibacillus plantarum BS3-1, together with associated temporal transcriptional changes in BS3-1 and metabolite variation in the fermentation broth, remain insufficiently characterized. Here, BS3-1 was evaluated across a 0-7% (w/w) salt gradient during suansun fermentation. The 0%, 3%, and 5% treatments were selected for time-series transcriptomic analysis of fermentation-derived cell pellets and untargeted metabolomic analysis of fermentation-broth supernatants. The 3% treatment yielded the highest sensory score (79.0/100 versus 72.2/100 in the no-added-salt treatment). On day 7, total acidity was 8.16 g/L at 1% salt and 3.60 g/L at 7%, and viable cells at 7% fell below the detection limit. BS3-1 transcriptional profiles and fermentation-broth metabolite compositions differed among salt treatments. In the 3% versus 0% comparison, 119 differentially expressed genes were shared across four time points, while an average of 598 differential metabolites was identified per time point. WGCNA identified 17 co-expression modules with significant module-trait associations. Association analysis integrating 126 candidate hub genes from four phenotype-associated modules with 30 shared differential metabolites retained 1100 gene-metabolite associations (|r| ≥ 0.65, global BH-FDR < 0.05). Overall, under the tested conditions, 3% salt provided the most favorable balance among viable-cell persistence, acidification, and sensory quality, while multi-omics analysis revealed covariation among BS3-1 transcriptional responses, fermentation traits, and fermentation-broth metabolite variation.

title: MSRepaint: Multiple Sclerosis Repaint with conditional denoising diffusion implicit model for bidirectional lesion filling and synthesis.
authors: Zhang J, Zuo L, Liu Y, Zhang H, Remedios SW, Landman BA, Calabresi PA, Saidha S
abstract: In multiple sclerosis (MS), lesions interfere with automated magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) analyses such as brain parcellation and deformable registration, while lesion segmentation models are hindered by the limited availability of annotated training data. To address both issues, we propose MSRepaint, a unified diffusion-based generative model for bidirectional lesion filling and synthesis that restores anatomical continuity for downstream analyses and augments segmentation through realistic data generation. MSRepaint conditions on spatial lesion masks for voxel-level control, incorporates contrast dropout to handle missing inputs, integrates a repainting mechanism to preserve surrounding anatomy during lesion filling and synthesis, and employs a multi-view DDIM inversion and fusion pipeline for 3D consistency with fast inference. Extensive evaluations demonstrate the effectiveness of MSRepaint across multiple tasks. For lesion filling, we evaluate both the accuracy within the filled regions and the impact on downstream tasks including brain parcellation and deformable registration. MSRepaint outperforms the FSL and NiftySeg lesion filling methods, and achieves accuracy on par with FastSurfer-LIT, a recent diffusion model-based lesion filling method, while offering over 20×faster inference. For lesion synthesis, state-of-the-art MS lesion segmentation models trained on MSRepaint-synthesized data outperform those trained on CarveMix-synthesized data or real ISBI challenge training data across multiple benchmarks, including the MICCAI 2016 and UMCL datasets. Additionally, we demonstrate that MSRepaint's unified bidirectional filling and synthesis capability, with full spatial control over lesion appearance, enables high-fidelity mask-conditioned voxel-wise control of lesion appearance within a unified framework. Our code is available at https://github.com/Jinwei1209/msrepaint.

title: Alzheimer's disease-associated presenilin 2 N141I mutation impairs neuronal lipid homeostasis and mitochondrial dynamics through selective downregulation of the Golgi exchange factor Gbf1.
authors: Saleki S, Wabant C, Loriot A, Stanga S, Masquelier J, Muccioli GG, Suelves N, Kienlen-Campard P
abstract: Presenilin 2 (PS2) mutations cause familial Alzheimer's disease, yet their effects beyond amyloid processing remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated how PS2 deletion and the N141I mutation affect neuronal lipid homeostasis and mitochondrial dynamics in mouse primary neurons. Both PS2 deletion and N141I mutation reduced neuronal lipid content. However, exogenous lipid supplementation rescued this deficit only in N141I-expressing neurons, indicating a partial loss-of-function effect. N141I neurons also displayed reduced OPA1, a mitochondrial fusion regulator, restored by lipid supplementation. RNA-sequencing identified Gbf1, a Golgi-specific guanine nucleotide exchange factor, as selectively downregulated in N141I but not knockout tissue, which was confirmed at the protein level in mouse brain and primary neurons. Gbf1 knockdown in mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs) recapitulated the N141I lipid profile. Together, these findings reveal a PS2-GBF1-lipid-mitochondria axis disrupted specifically by the N141I mutation, suggesting an amyloid-independent pathway contributing to neurodegeneration and identifying potential therapeutic targets for familial Alzheimer's disease.

title: Synthesis and pharmacological evaluation of a series of fluoro-substituted 3-phenoxy-azetidines as cortical enhancers for the treatment of apathy.
authors: Sonesson C, von Unge S, Gullme M, Rousk L, Fagerberg A, Knubbe T, Svanberg B, Ljung E
abstract: We here report the discovery of a series of fluoro-substituted 3-phenoxy-azetidines useful for modulating levels of monoamines in cerebral cortical areas of the brain. The compounds were characterized by in vivo studies using, in particular, behavioural, and microdialysis methods. Furthermore, the compounds were tested in binding assays for the human serotonin (5-HT), noradrenaline (NA), and dopamine (DA) transporters in order to assess the risk for addiction/dependency. Optimization of this class of compounds for improving cognitive functions while minimizing the effect on monoamine transporters resulted in the selection of a candidate drug 1 (IRL757). After 1 was successfully assessed in different animal models for motivation/goal-directed behaviour (unpublished data), it is currently being evaluated in humans for the treatment of apathy in neurological disorders in general, and in particular in Parkinson's disease (PD).

title: Cytotoxic T lymphocyte-inspired nanotherapeutics chaperoning granzyme B for tumor immune remodeling.
authors: Chen Y, Zhang Y, Chen J, Du X, Wang S, Ma Z, Zhou H, Yu J
abstract: T cell-based cancer immunotherapies have transformed oncology; however, their clinical benefit remains limited in immunologically cold tumors, where poor T cell infiltration and impaired effector function weaken endogenous tumor cell killing. Here, we developed GrB@A-nChap, a cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL)-inspired nanotherapeutic that chaperones granzyme B (GrB) into the tumor cell cytosol to supplement deficient cytotoxic effector activity in "cold" tumors. Mechanistically, GrB@A-nChap protects GrB under physiological conditions, undergoes partial protonation in the mildly acidic tumor microenvironment to enhance tumor cell uptake, and further responds to lysosomal acidity to promote acidity-dependent lysosomal escape and cytosolic GrB release. Cytosolic GrB then induces mitochondrial dysfunction, caspase-3 activation, and GSDME cleavage, thereby triggering an apoptosis-pyroptosis cascade. This cell death process is accompanied by ICD-associated molecular signals and enhanced dendritic cell maturation. In vivo, GrB@A-nChap treatment was associated with increased intratumoral immune cell infiltration and local immune modulation and enhanced the therapeutic response to αPD-1 treatment. This work establishes a CTLinspired nanotherapeutic that enables cytosolic GrB delivery and provides cell independent GrB-mediated tumor cell killing, offering a potential strategy for complementing existing treatments for cold tumors.
